summary: Twitter/X Developer API access has become significantly more restrictive since 2023. Free tier access is extremely limited (1,500 tweets/month write). Basic access (paid, ~$100/month) is needed for most practical integrations. Elevated access requires manual review. The OAuth 2.0 setup itself is straightforward — the bottleneck is the access tier approval and the ongoing cost. Your app needs to explain exactly what it does in the developer portal.
key_facts: Free Developer Account: 1,500 tweet writes/month, 10,000 reads/month — very limited
Basic plan ($100/month): 3M tweet reads/month — needed for most real applications
Pro plan ($5,000/month) and Enterprise tiers exist for high-volume use
OAuth 2.0 (PKCE) is available for user-context actions; OAuth 1.0a still used for some endpoints
App must be approved before getting production credentials — developer portal review
Composio managed auth available, but your users need to authorize your app with their own accounts
API v1.1 endpoints are being deprecated — use v2 API

steps.title: Apply for Developer Access
steps.description: Go to developer.twitter.com and sign in with your Twitter/X account. Apply for developer access by describing your use case. You must explain: what you're building, how you'll use the API, whether you'll display tweets outside Twitter, and whether you'll analyze data.
warnings: Be specific and honest — vague answers cause delays or rejection
Mentioning automation should be tied to clear user-serving purposes

steps.title: Select Access Tier
steps.description: Choose your access tier: Free (very limited), Basic ($100/month), Pro ($5,000/month), or Enterprise. For most Composio integrations enabling user actions (reading timeline, posting tweets), Basic is the minimum practical tier.
warnings: Free tier is insufficient for most real applications — budget for at least Basic ($100/month)

steps.title: Create a Project and App
steps.description: In the Developer Portal, create a Project (container) and then create an App inside it. Configure: App name, description, app website URL, callback URLs. For Composio: https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback

steps.title: Configure OAuth 2.0
steps.description: In your App settings, go to 'User authentication settings'. Enable OAuth 2.0. Set Type of App (Web App/Native App). Add callback URLs and website URL. Select required scopes (tweet.read, tweet.write, users.read, offline.access for refresh tokens).
warnings: offline.access scope is required if you want refresh tokens for long-lived access

steps.title: Get API Keys and Configure Composio
steps.description: From App settings → Keys and tokens: get Client ID and Client Secret (for OAuth 2.0). Configure in Composio custom auth config with toolkit='twitter'.

requirements.account_type: Twitter/X account + Developer Portal approval + paid plan for real usage

blockers.title: Paid Tier Required for Practical Use
blockers.description: The Free tier limits of 1,500 tweets/month write and 10,000 reads/month make it insufficient for any real user-facing application. Basic plan costs $100/month.
blockers.workaround: Budget for at least the Basic tier ($100/month). Evaluate if Twitter/X integration is worth the ongoing cost vs. user value.

blockers.title: Developer Portal Approval
blockers.description: Applications must describe their use case in the Developer Portal. Automated, spam, or unclear use cases are rejected.
blockers.workaround: Prepare a clear, detailed use-case description focusing on genuine user value, not automation.
